Improving veteran care starts with cutting bureaucratic bloat, not just budget theatrics. While partnerships matter, real progress requires audits to redirect funds from administrative waste to frontline services. The VA’s $2.3B mental health spend and $588M suicide prevention efforts must face scrutiny—too often, cash gets lost in layers of bureaucracy instead of reaching vets.

Streamlining community care referrals and modernizing health records are steps forward, but let’s see if this “reorganization” actually trims fat or just shuffles deck chairs.

Veterans deserve care that’s efficient, not entangled in red tape.
